searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's. Four were restricted to a producer or wine body domain (bbvwine.com, hortonwine.com with Wikipedia, lindenvineyards.com twice, virginiawine.org with missouriwine.org, chrysaliswine.com with Middleburg Life) and read as primary for the house's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on one source or none was cut or hedged as the house's claim; every glass note was rewritten from tasting notes found.

tested: Octagon first vintage and its commercial start: Washingtonian, Wine and Country Life, C-Ville, Decanter; 1991, 1995, and 1998 in quantity.
The founding of 1976 against advice to plant tobacco and early plantings: the house Heritage page, Boomer Magazine, Bend Bulletin; the Cabernet Franc claim unsupported.
Zonin firm of 1821 and the one estate outside Italy: Broadbent, Wikipedia, a Zonin1821 piece.
Petit Verdot Reserve 2010 and the Monticello Cup: C-Ville snippet unclear; cut.
Making: the house page for the 2021 (six to ten days, twelve months in barriques, part new, six months steel).
Glass and blend: Suckling notes of 2013, 2016, 2018; RJonWine 2002; Jancis Robinson 2007 blend Cabernet Sauvignon led; Decanter 2014 Monticello.
The house, its design about 1822 and the fire of Christmas Day 1884: Virginia DHR, Monticello encyclopedia, Wikipedia.
changed: story: was that the house led the state in planting Cabernet Franc in 1976; now cut, since no source read supports it and the early plantings named are Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Chardonnay.

story: was Octagon first made in 1991 from young plantings, its modern shape from 1997 and the 2019 the twenty first; now 1991 from older plantings, again 1995, and the 1998 the first made in quantity, by the Washingtonian and Wine and Country Life; the count of Octagons found in no source and cut.

story: was the Barbour family farming into the twentieth century and local advice to plant tobacco; now the house's account that officials and bankers advised tobacco, and the farming line cut for want of a source.
wine.grapes and the question's explanation: was Merlot the larger part in most vintages; now in most vintages read, with Cabernet Sauvignon leading the 2007 by Jancis Robinson's record.
wine.making: was about a week on skins and some months in steel; now six to ten days and about six months, by the house's page for the 2021.
wine.glass: was the house's note alone; now blackcurrant, raspberry, blueberry, cedar, sweet tobacco and toasty oak, as tastings of 2002, 2013, 2015 and 2016 give them.
wine.label: Virginia now says some vintages carry the Monticello AVA, as Decanter's record of the 2014 does.
others: the Petit Verdot Reserve's Monticello Cup of 2010 cut, confirmed in no source read.
sources: one source gives way to the Washingtonian page that carries a fact now taught.
open: Whether Octagon first came in quantity with the 1997 or the 1998 differs between one interview and the Washingtonian; the record teaches 1998.
One report of 2026 of a creditor procedure at Zonin1821 and a sale of the estate was met in one source and is not taught.

Governor's Cup 2019 for the 2016 Petit Manseng, the first Petit Manseng overall winner: the Governor's release.

Norton back to Virginia in 1989: Virginia Wine pages.
Glass: Vinovoss, FirstLeaf, Enjoying Viognier, Delectable notes of 2015 and 2017.
changed: story: was the land bought in 1988; now 1989 by the house's own account, after a home vineyard in Madison County from 1983.

story, table: was the 1993 Viognier taking first place at a California tasting; now the 1992 Viognier winning its class at the San Diego National Wine Competition of 1994, by the house's medal list, which shows the 1993 with silver and bronze only.
story and question: was the first commercial planting of Norton in Virginia since Prohibition; now brought back to Virginia from Missouri in 1989, as Virginia Wine tells it.
others: Norton's port style wine cut, found in no source read.
wine.glass: was green apple and peach untested; now apricot, peach, honeysuckle, gardenia and a hint of ginger, as several notes of 2015 to 2017 give them.
sources: one source gives way to the Horton Vineyards page that carries a fact now taught.

tested: The orchard of 1983, planting of 1985, first vintage 1987, 1,350 feet: the house About and Hardscrabble pages.

Making by vintage 1998 to 2015: the house notes.

story: the malolactic of the late 1990s now dated (partial 1998, none 1999, full 2000) and the tank start of 2012, by the house's notes.
wine.glass: was lemon, green apple and a saline edge untested; now wet stone, tart apple, lemon and pear, gaining hazelnut and honey, by the house's notes and published tastings.

story, label and card: was Lost Mountain the low range between the Blue Ridge and Bull Run; now named for the place where it grows, as the press gives it; the range found in no source.
story and label: was the old logo kept after the sale; now cut, in one report only.

story: the land once labelled not suitable for agriculture, by the Washington Post, and the house that under its founder made two wines, since the new owners announced new wines.

sources: one source gives way to the Virginia Living page that carries a fact now taught.

livingNamesMet: Barboursville: the founder of 1976 Gianni Zonin and the winemaker Luca Paschina.
Horton: the founder's widow Sharon Horton; the founder Dennis Horton is dead (2018) but undated and not named.
Linden: the founder Jim Law and the manager Shari Avenius, whose surname names a vineyard and stands as a place.
RdV: the founder Rutger de Vink, the consultant Eric Boissenot, the winemaker Joshua Grainer, the chief executive Pierre Graffeuille, the adviser Kees van Leeuwen, the Bouygues brothers.
Chrysalis: the founder Jennifer McCloud and the consultant Alan Kinne.
Critics met in sources: Jancis Robinson, James Suckling, Jane Anson; none is named in the fragment. The read-together agent may add these names to people.json.
swaps: No swap proposed by the author. The refuter rules all five picks stand. The author's note that RdV is renamed Lost Mountain Vineyards is no swap: it is the same house, so the read-together agent or the integrator may relabel the producer in plan.json without a new key; the refuter recommends no change of key.
codexTension: The region summary calls Viognier promoted as the signature grape since 2011, which the records agree with. The region producers line for Barboursville speaks of Jefferson's design and its 1976 founding, both confirmed. No library record exists for any of the five houses. No Codex record was edited.
